**Use the coding agents you already pay for, in one workspace.**

JAM Code is a free, open-source desktop workspace for coding agents such as
Claude Code and Codex. It puts your projects, agent conversations, Git
worktrees, files, terminal, browser and code review in one window. See it at
[code.jaym.tech](https://code.jaym.tech).

This is the first public **alpha**, for technical early adopters: it works, it
has rough edges, and it may change in incompatible ways.

## What's in it

- **Claude Code and Codex chats** with streaming replies, tool activity and
  diffs as readable cards, inline approvals and questions, stop and resume,
  and model, effort and access choices.
- **Projects from folders.** Any folder can be a project; Git is optional.
  Removing a project never touches its files.
- **Worktree chats.** Start a chat in the current checkout or in a new Git
  worktree on its own branch, so parallel chats never edit the same files.
- **Searchable history** across every conversation.
- **Tabs and tiled panes**: any chat, terminal, file, browser or review in
  any pane.
- **Terminal**, a **Browser** with element and region annotations you can
  attach to a chat, a **file browser** with Markdown preview, and **Git
  review** with stage and unstage.
- **Appearance**: themes, accents, fonts, backgrounds and keybindings.
- **Snapshots** (macOS): capture a window into a chat's composer.

## Before you install

- **Windows 11 (x64)** or **macOS 14+** (one universal build). Windows 10 and
  Intel Macs are untested. There is no Linux build yet.
- Install [Claude Code](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code),
  [Codex](https://github.com/openai/codex) or both, and sign in with their own
  CLIs. JAM Code uses those installations and never asks for your provider
  credentials. Details:
  [PROVIDERS.md](https://github.com/jayamartinez/jam-code/blob/main/docs/PROVIDERS.md).

## Installing an unsigned build

Alpha installers are not code-signed, so your system asks before the first
launch.

- **Windows:** SmartScreen shows "Windows protected your PC". Choose
  _More info → Run anyway_.
- **macOS:** the app is not notarized. Open it once, then choose _Open
  Anyway_ in _System Settings → Privacy & Security_ (on macOS 14, right-click
  the app → _Open_). If macOS says the app is damaged, run
  `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/JAM Code.app"`.

You can check downloads against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

## Known limitations

- Files open read-only; agents make the edits.
- No automatic updates, and no import of history from the providers' own apps.
- The Browser has no devtools and agents cannot control it.
- Snapshots are macOS-only.
- Quitting interrupts running chats; they can be resumed afterwards.
- The packaged macOS build has had less hands-on testing than the Windows one.
